lens: COMPARISON VALIDITY AND FEASIBILITY (round 2 verification of plan_v2 P4.0-P4.10 against the P4.11 log and round-1 V1-V12, F1-F14)

unresolved_round1.why_unresolved: D7 says 'the loop's at_config evaluator applies THEIR exact test', but today's loop has no evaluator: after every move it names the readback after the target (test_full_pipeline.py:1594-1597, current_config = RobotConfig(actual_joints, name=q2.name)), so at_config(target) is asserted whatever the error. pick, place and stack require (at_config ?q) of a kinematic config (pddl/domain_pddlstream.pddl:242, 283, 359), and the executor settles only to 2e-3 rad (robot_utils.py:778-781). An evaluator applied to every config therefore fails every pick precondition and re-creates the F5 livelock on kin configs, where the home_not_reached bound does not apply. The plan never states the evaluator's scope, which symbol the readback receives when the test fails, and B3 does not list the evaluator at all (B3(d) names only 'the goal-configuration final hold'), so it would land in the main loop without its own A/B.
unresolved_round1.required_change: D7 and B3(d): the 1e-4 evaluator applies ONLY to the declared goal configuration q_home; every other move keeps today's name-on-arrival rule. When the test fails, current_config becomes a fresh Config symbol carrying the readback joints (never named q_home). List the evaluator in B3 as a loop change with default off and run the B3 A/B on it.

unresolved_round1.why_unresolved: Only the plan-count half was fixed. B3 still demands 'identical per-seed outcomes and identical Phase-4 target choices' over 40 seeds, and B5 and M6 reuse that acceptance ('A/B as in B3'). The project's own measurement (PAPER_AUDIT.txt:2512-2522) shows identical planning code flipping 3 of 20 seeds from wall-clock noise, and P4.6 itself calls +/-1-2 seeds per 20 the noise floor. A pure refactor will therefore fail B3 on noise, which pushes the implementer to re-run until it passes or to loosen the criterion after the fact.
unresolved_round1.required_change: Pre-register the same rule for outcomes as for plan counts: a per-seed outcome flip fails only if one pre-registered re-run of that seed on BOTH arms reproduces it, and the number of re-runs is fixed before the A/B starts. Alternatively, gate against an A/A run of c31cbdd under the arm-O interpreter and accept flips up to the A/A count. Target-choice identity stays exact, because it is decided before any wall-clock search.

unresolved_round1.why_unresolved: Masses and settle logging were adopted, but the disclosure was copied wrongly and the die was left out. D9 and P4.6 say TAMPURA's 'bodies float 1 cm above the table for the whole episode'. In fact the die sits at the cup's centre point: z 0.0493 in 1747173591 and z 0.0523 in 1747173593, against a resting z of about 0.0109 (0.0209 minus the generator's +0.01). So in 12 of 20 seeds (7 + 5) TAMPURA's die floats about 3.8 to 4.1 cm up inside the cup, and TAMPURA picks a die in mid air while ours must pick it off the table (map_tampura.json claim at line 15; env_generator.py:117, 126-127). The pre-registered disclosure covers only cups that move more than 1 cm. Nothing checks that the die is still hidden after the settle. Nothing fixes whether the first render comes before or after the settle; if it comes before, the boxels are built on poses that are 1 cm too high.
unresolved_round1.required_change: Correct the D9 and P4.6 disclosure to say that TAMPURA's die floats inside the cup at cup-centre height in layouts ...91 and ...93 for its whole episode. Pre-register the order: D9 dynamics, then settle N steps, then the first render. After the settle, assert that the die is absent from the D4 eye's segmentation. If it is visible, flag the episode scene_changed_by_settle and report it in its own row of the per-seed table, never re-seated or re-rolled. Log the die's displacement alongside the cups'.

unresolved_round1.why_unresolved: The calendar still quotes 'the 21 days summed here', which is draft 1's sum. The revised per-package efforts add up to 26 to 32 agent-days, or 34 with M6, between 2026-10-26 and the B8 date of 2026-11-30 (35 calendar days). No days are budgeted for the four agent review gates in P4.1. At the upper estimates, the 11-17 milestone (B4-B6 in 5 days for 5 to 10 days of work) misses even if everything before it is on time. Missing the 11-20 go/no-go is therefore the expected case, and the fallback becomes the likely outcome.
unresolved_round1.required_change: Recompute the sum from the revised efforts. Add review-gate days. Name the latest B8 start date that still fits the paper deadline. Pre-register a cut order that touches no comparison-validity item, for example B9 and the optional view-blocking count first. See the new finding on defining 'clean'.

unresolved_round1.why_unresolved: B3(f) fixes the interpreter but adds 'scipy, trimesh, imageio and pyyaml' to wsl_env without pinning versions. In arm O, THEIR scene construction also runs in OUR interpreter, and create_ycb offsets every body's collision and visual geometry by trimesh's mesh.center_mass (panda_env_utils.py:688-691). A different trimesh version can therefore move the geometry of the die and the cups relative to the JSON poses, in arm O only. Their code is also untested on numpy 2.2.6 (for example pb_utils.py:1781 uses np.array(..., copy=False), whose meaning changed in NumPy 2). No step checks that the two interpreters build the same scene.
unresolved_round1.required_change: Pin trimesh, scipy and imageio in wsl_env to their venv's exact versions (trimesh 4.12.2 and scipy 1.15.3 per the round-1 feasibility evidence) and record them in campaign.json. Add to B1 an assertion that, for all three layouts, the per-body AABBs and the t=0 segmentation id set are identical under both interpreters before any O episode runs.

new_findings.title: TAMPURA's find_dice world has no gravity, the adopt-client path skips our only setGravity, and the plan never mentions gravity
new_findings.plan_location: P4.3 D9 ('Nothing else of theirs is altered'), P4.4 B1(c), B3(b), G1/G14
new_findings.problem: find_dice and panda_env_utils never call setGravity. setup_robot_pybullet creates the BulletClient, configures the GUI and loads the robot, and nothing else. PyBullet's default gravity is zero. Our BoxelTestEnv sets gravity only at boxel_env.py:511, right after resetSimulation at :510, and that is exactly the block B3(b)'s adopt-existing-client path omits ('no resetSimulation, no _setup_scene'). With D9's masses but no gravity, nothing settles, the die keeps floating at cup-centre height, and a released cup never falls, so _release_and_verify_drop cannot pass. Either every place fails (a 0/20 caused by the harness) or an implementer adds setGravity silently, perhaps in the B1(c) probe but not in the bridge, so the settle numbers would not describe the campaign. Either way it is an unrecorded change to their world.
new_findings.evidence: grep of tampura_environments for setGravity: only class_uncertain/env.py:334, puck_slide/env.py:258 and tool_use/env.py:308; panda_env_utils.py:844-851 (setup_robot_pybullet, no gravity); find_dice/env.py:816-876 (initialize, no gravity); boxel_env.py:510-511 (resetSimulation then setGravity(0,0,-9.81), the block B3(b) skips); plan D9 'Nothing else of theirs is altered'; no occurrence of 'gravity' anywhere in plan_v2.txt
new_findings.required_change: D9: declare one setGravity(0, 0, -9.81) call on the executing client (our pipeline's value, boxel_env.py:511) before the first step. Record it in its own BF# entry, allowlist it, and add setGravity, setTimeStep and setPhysicsEngineParameter on the executing client to the G14 trap. The B1(c) settle probe must use the identical call sequence. P4.6 discloses that their world runs without gravity, so T's bodies stay where the JSON put them, while ours fall under gravity.

new_findings.title: With M1, q_clear IS q_home, so the 1e-4 test and the home_not_reached bound gate every sense and can end an episode in mid-search
new_findings.plan_location: P4.3 D5 ('one object, two roles'), D7 (final hold, home_not_reached), B1(i), B4
new_findings.problem: D5 makes the clearance configuration the same symbol as q_home. D7 applies their allclose (about 1e-4 to 3.7e-4 rad per joint) to the at_config evaluation of q_home, gives moves to it a final hold, and ends the episode after 'two consecutive moves to q_home that leave the evaluator false'. Once M1 is adopted, every sense is preceded by a move to q_home with an empty hand. A readback 2e-4 rad off then blocks the sense precondition, the planner plans a near-zero move home, and the second miss ends the episode as home_not_reached, during SEARCH, for a precision that is irrelevant to arm clearance, which is a 2 cm geometric question. B1(i) measures convergence only while holding a die-mass body, not empty-handed from the post-place poses M1 starts from. Because B1(h)'s rule takes the WORST blocked fraction over every window cell with the arm at a post-place lift pose, and the eye sits where the hand rests at home behind the arm's reach, M1 will almost certainly be adopted. The coupling is therefore the expected case, not an edge case.
new_findings.evidence: plan D5 'q_clear = DEFAULT_ARM_POS, which IS the planner's home_config symbol (one object, two roles)'; plan D7 'two consecutive moves to q_home that leave the evaluator false end the episode with exit reason home_not_reached'; find_dice/env.py:318-320 (allclose rtol=atol=1e-4); robot_utils.py:778-781 (today's hold stops at 2e-3)
new_findings.required_change: Separate the roles. q_clear is its own Config object with DEFAULT_ARM_POS joints and today's name-on-arrival semantics, or an explicit geometric tolerance. The 1e-4 evaluator, the final hold to that tolerance and home_not_reached apply only to the goal conjunct at_config(q_home) reached while holding. B1(i) also measures empty-hand convergence from post-place poses. Record in BF# that M1 adoption is expected from B1(h)'s worst-case rule.

new_findings.title: The fallback's trigger 'B7 is not clean' is undefined, so it can suppress an unfavourable same-task result
new_findings.problem: If B7 is 'not clean' by 2026-11-20, the fallback says the paper 'reports no bridge numbers' and keeps the indirect comparison. 'Clean' is defined nowhere. B7 runs watched episodes that produce rewards, so 'not clean' can be read as 'our arm failed the watched seeds'. That reading turns the fallback into selective reporting: run the same-task comparison, and publish it only if it looks good. Given the calendar arithmetic (see F9), the fallback is the likely branch, so its trigger decides what the paper says about the comparison the user asked for ('see who did better').
new_findings.evidence: plan P4.4 'FALLBACK if B7 is not clean by 2026-11-20: the paper keeps the thesis's indirect comparison ... and reports no bridge numbers'; B7 'Abort: any gate red; any temptation to add a helper motion, retry or fallback' (abort conditions, not a definition of clean); P4.0 user request 'see who did better, how quickly'
new_findings.required_change: Pre-register 'clean' by process criteria only: G1-G20 green, the G6 positive and negative controls pass, and both watched episodes reach a logged exit reason with no harness exception. Rewards never enter the definition. If clean, B8 runs and is reported whatever the outcome, including after 11-20 if it still fits before the deadline (state that date). If not clean, the paper states that a seed-for-seed run on TAMPURA's environment was attempted and names the blocking BF#. B7's raw outcomes are recorded in BF# either way, and the indirect comparison carries only the P4.5 corrected wording.

new_findings.title: D11 decides cup graspability on MESH widths while the sampler gates on PERCEIVED widths, and the one measurement of detector error is barred from the decision
new_findings.problem: D11 branch (i) runs the sampler unchanged if the d and e class widths measured from the mesh fit GRASP_MAX_SPAN. At run time, sample_grasp compares the pinch span of the ESTIMATED box with 0.076. Depth-based AABBs overestimate by several millimetres, and the cups are wide where the AABB is taken (the rim). A class within a few millimetres of the span passes D11 but is refused at run time, which gives no_grasp_in_span on every seed of the affected layouts. That is exactly the 0/20 by construction R1 and D11 exist to prevent. B1(e) measures our detector's AABB error, but only for the die and 'for the disclosures only'.
new_findings.evidence: plan D11 '(i) If the d and e class widths fit GRASP_MAX_SPAN, the sampler runs unchanged'; plan B1(e) '... our detector's AABB error ... feeds no constant and no camera choice'; streams.py:726 (grasps 'over its ESTIMATED box'), :719 (GRASP_MAX_SPAN = 0.076), :819 (span > GRASP_MAX_SPAN skipped)
new_findings.required_change: B1(e) also records, for every cup in the three t=0 renders, or on a neutral table at the eye's viewing geometry, our estimated pinch extent next to the mesh width. D11 branch (i) requires the maximum ESTIMATED width per class to be at most GRASP_MAX_SPAN, and otherwise takes branch (ii). This is a class-level decision from a perception measurement, not from an episode outcome.

new_findings.title: D4 and D8 leave out the view construction, the near plane, the robot's own occlusion at home and partly framed cups
new_findings.plan_location: P4.3 D4, D6 STATUS RULE, D8 window, G20, B1(e)
new_findings.problem: (a) Their render builds the view from eye = camera_frame position, target = pose * [0,0,5], up = world +z, near 0.02, far 5.0. Ours defaults to near 0.01 and takes its up vector from the env. D4 fixes only 'their intrinsics', so G20 can pass while the image differs from their generator's hidden check (roll, robot geometry 1 to 2 cm from the lens). (b) D8 intersects free space with the TABLE-PLANE frustum footprint. A cell or a placed cup near the footprint edge leaves the frame at its top, because the frustum's cross-section shrinks towards the camera. The hand is in frame at home (D4 says so) and occludes table cells our free-space model still counts as observed. Both cases contradict D6's justification that 'free cells are observed space'. (c) The generator requires only an object's centre to project into the image, so a hiding d or e cup can be partly out of frame. B1(e) measures the in-frame fraction, but neither the disclosure list nor the per-seed table carries it.
new_findings.evidence: pb_utils.py:1836-1837 (near 0.02, far 5.0), :1844 (up [0,0,1]), :1895-1908 (target along camera +z at far); boxel_env.py:445 (near_plane 0.01), :1622-1631 (computeViewMatrix with self.camera_up); env_generator.py:131-148 (only the centre point is tested); plan D8 '... with the D4 eye's table-plane frustum footprint, so free space is observed space'; plan D4 'When the arm is at home its hand is in frame'
new_findings.required_change: D4 and G20 declare eye, target, up, near and far exactly as get_image_at_pose computes them, and G20 compares against matrices produced by their own pbu path. D8's window keeps only table cells whose column up to the tallest declared class height projects entirely into the frame and is free of robot pixels in the t=0 home render. P4.6's disclosures list, per layout, every cup with an in-frame fraction below 1.

new_findings.title: tampura_policy_timed cannot time env.step without a monkeypatch or a rollout copy, T must run from our own driver, and 'agree within the noise floor' is unmeasured
new_findings.plan_location: P4.6 ARMS, TIME (t5); G13; G19; B2
new_findings.problem: Policy.rollout calls self.get_action and then env.step directly. Wrapping env.step therefore needs either an instance patch, which G13's 'no monkeypatch' forbids, or an overridden rollout, which re-implements their loop. Registration has to happen in the process, so T can no longer run through run_planner.py or tampura_sweep.py as shipped: our driver must reproduce run_planner's __main__ exactly (seeding, logger, env, initialize, policy, rollout) and must not consume the global RNG, but G19's RNG clause is written for O only. 'Agree within the noise floor' with B1(g) has no criterion, T's own run-to-run variation has never been measured, and PYTHONHASHSEED is recorded only for O. Subclassing and the registry name change nothing else: grep finds no other use of the planner name in tampura, and run_planner.py:135 is the only lookup. G13 asserts 'exactly two registrations', yet B2 'registers the schema and BoxelBridgePolicy', which makes three if the policy goes through register_planner.
new_findings.evidence: tampura/policies/policy.py:120, 129 (get_action, then env.step); run_planner.py:101-138 (__main__ only); tampura/policies/__init__.py:15 and config.py:47-52 (the only registry use); plan G13 'Exactly two runtime registrations ... No monkeypatch of their classes'; plan B2 'registers the schema and BoxelBridgePolicy'
new_findings.required_change: The subclass wraps only get_action. The step+update share is time_deltas[k] - time_deltas[k-1] minus get_action_k. The T driver is run_planner.py's __main__ copied line for line plus one import, kept identical by a gate diff, with G19 applied to it. BoxelBridgePolicy is instantiated directly, or G13 counts three. Pin the same PYTHONHASHSEED for B1(g), both T repetitions and O. Pre-register agreement: timed T per-seed outcomes may differ from B1(g) only on seeds that also flipped between the 2026-05-26 block and B1(g); otherwise both blocks are reported and neither is chosen. Optional symmetric column: T successes where env.state.current_q is not at DEFAULT_ARM_POS (their go-home reports home on a failed motion plan), read only.

new_findings.title: D3 store-symbol scoring works, but the grasp record and execute_fn's return values must be plain data, because the rollout deep-copies and pickles them
new_findings.problem: D3 is verified sound. add_typed after initialize only inserts into als and als_type. get_reward reads abstract facts plus type_dict, and the Exists ranges over 'physical' only. verify runs once at rollout start, before our symbol exists. update copies grasp and grasp_body when grasp is not None. However, the rollout deep-copies the store and env.state at every one of the 20 steps and pickles the whole history at the end. '<our grasp record>' is unspecified: a record holding a client, our env or a class from tampura_bridge makes every step's deepcopy heavy, or makes the pickle unloadable without our package. The same applies to the state execute_fn returns and to the info dict.
new_findings.evidence: tampura/store.py:59-63 (add_typed stores the object as is); tampura/spec.py:140-143 (get_reward), :235-270 (verify); tampura/policies/policy.py:66 (deepcopy(store) per step), :99 (verify once), :106 (deepcopy(env.state) per step), :159 (pickle.dump(history)); find_dice/env.py:297-302, 306-323
new_findings.required_change: Specify the grasp value as a plain tuple of floats (position, quaternion, width). execute_fn returns the SceneState object it received. The policy's info dict holds only JSON-able values, and the ledger lives in our files. G6 adds a test that the RolloutHistory pickle loads in their venv without tampura_bridge on PYTHONPATH.
